scientific_hypothesis: A two-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter using Germanium (high-index) and Zinc Sulfide (low-index) dielectric materials on CaF2 substrate can achieve high transmittance in both CO (4.55-4.75 μm) and CO2 (4.15-4.35 μm) bands while blocking 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm, with total layer count ≤24.
expected_advantages: Ge/ZnS pair has high index contrast (~4.0 vs ~2.2 in mid-IR) enabling fewer layers for required blocking
Dielectric-only design avoids metal absorption losses (15-30% reduction in transmittance)
19 layers leaves margin under 24-layer constraint for optimization flexibility
known_risks: Ge has absorption edge near 1.8 μm but should be transparent in 3.5-5.2 μm range - must verify dispersion model
Stress mismatch between Ge and ZnS may cause film cracking if total thickness exceeds practical limits
Fabrication tolerance sensitivity increases with layer count and index contrast
expected_observations: best_target_score should increase as cavity thicknesses approach half-wave resonance at target wavelengths
tightest_margin should improve as mirror stack reflectivity increases in stopband regions
valid_candidates may decrease if cavity coupling causes unrealistic thickness requirements
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if tightest_margin becomes negative for five consecutive rounds, reduce cavity layer count by one pair and restart optimization
